sessions.phase_label: Report scope, design references, and deliverable planning
Initial concept review and presentation refinements
Canva conversion, multi-format delivery, and design-asset handoff

requirements.title: Consistent Reference-Based Visual Theme
requirements.definition: Apply the supplied design reference as a consistent, polished, premium visual theme across all report variants.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the shared visual language across reports; section-specific dashboard, header, footer, and warning behavior remains in separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Prominent Front-Page Result Summary
requirements.definition: Present the vehicle security score and principal risk outcome prominently on the first page so customers can understand the result immediately.
requirements.boundary_note: Includes score prominence, the Vehicle Security Score label, risk band, exposure level, priority level, and dashboard spacing; result causes and weaknesses are independently scannable content.

requirements.title: Scannable Front-Page Result Drivers
requirements.definition: Show the main reason for the rating and primary security weaknesses on page one in a concise, easily scanned form.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the causes and weaknesses summary rather than the score and risk-result display; longer supporting explanations may remain elsewhere.

requirements.title: Clean Vehicle Identification Display
requirements.definition: Present the vehicle group or assessed vehicle as clean report information rather than as an unfinished checkbox form.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers how vehicle identity is displayed; the ability to edit the customer-specific value belongs to the separate field-editability Requirement.

requirements.title: Consistent Internal Page Headers
requirements.definition: Provide subtle, consistent headers on internal pages containing the appropriate report identity and confidentiality information.
requirements.boundary_note: Header presence and presentation can change independently from footer behavior; correctness of the DX code itself is tracked under variant identifiers.

requirements.title: Consistent Report Footers
requirements.definition: Provide a clean, consistent footer on every report page, including the final page, with the required report metadata and page information.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers footer presence, consistency, and compatibility with other page elements; variant-specific code correctness is a separate Requirement.

requirements.title: Refined Confidential Distribution Warning
requirements.definition: Retain a clear confidentiality and limited-distribution warning while keeping it visually refined and subordinate to the rest of the final page.
requirements.boundary_note: The warning's visibility and styling form an independently reviewed final-page element; restoration of the page footer is handled separately.

requirements.title: Transparent Scoring Summary
requirements.definition: Include a clear scoring table showing each main scoring category, its maximum score, the customer score, and the total score.
requirements.boundary_note: The scoring table is independently assessable from the prominent front-page score and from recommendation content.

requirements.title: Prioritized Security Recommendations
requirements.definition: Present practical security recommendations as a prioritized upgrade path, including immediate actions, priority upgrades, and secondary upgrades.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the recommendation hierarchy and action-led structure, not variant-specific wording used to describe differing exposure levels.

requirements.title: Accurate Approved Core Report Copy
requirements.definition: Use the client-approved wording in shared report content and remove identified typos, placeholder prose, and awkward sentences.
requirements.boundary_note: Individual sentence corrections are attributes of one shared copy-accuracy obligation; wording deliberately differentiated by risk variant is tracked separately.

requirements.title: DX17–DX20 Risk-Based Variant Set
requirements.definition: Provide four distinct editable report variants—DX17, DX18, DX19, and DX20—so the appropriate template can be selected for a customer's score or risk level.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers existence and risk-based selection of the four variants; titles, identifiers, narrative wording, and delivery formats can fail or change independently.

requirements.title: Correct Variant Risk-Band Titles
requirements.definition: Assign the approved risk-band title to each report variant: Critical Risk for DX17, Heightened Risk for DX18, Moderate Risk for DX19, and Minimal Risk for DX20.
requirements.boundary_note: Risk-band titles have their own failure and correction trajectory, separate from report IDs and longer variant-specific narrative copy.

requirements.title: Consistent Variant-Specific Report Identifiers
requirements.definition: Ensure every report-detail field, header, and footer uses the DX code corresponding to its own report variant.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers identifier correctness across locations; it does not replace the independent requirements for header/footer presence or variant risk-band titles.

requirements.title: Risk-Appropriate Variant Narrative
requirements.definition: Use explanatory and recommendation wording appropriate to each variant's actual exposure level rather than reusing severe-risk language in lower-risk reports.
requirements.boundary_note: The approved sentences for individual variants are attributes of one risk-alignment behavior; generic shared-copy corrections remain separate.

requirements.title: Editable Customer-Specific Report Fields
requirements.definition: Allow the client to update customer-specific fields such as registration, assessment date, report ID, vehicle group, scores, risk band, weaknesses, recommendations, and notes.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers field-level editability and clean editable placeholders regardless of file platform; Word and Canva delivery are separate format Requirements.

requirements.title: Self-Service Customer-Ready PDF Export
requirements.definition: Enable the client to use the editable source templates to export future customer-ready PDF reports without further designer assistance.
requirements.boundary_note: Export capability of the editable sources is independently required from delivery of the project's already-exported final PDF files.

requirements.title: Editable Word Templates
requirements.definition: Provide editable Microsoft Word source versions of the completed DX17–DX20 report templates.
requirements.boundary_note: Word is one independently deliverable editable format; its successful delivery does not satisfy the separate Canva or final-PDF obligations.

requirements.title: Editable Canva Templates
requirements.definition: Provide accessible, editable Canva templates for DX17, DX18, DX19, and DX20.
requirements.boundary_note: Canva delivery has a distinct commitment and accessibility trajectory from the already supplied Word files.

requirements.title: Final PDF Exports
requirements.definition: Deliver final PDF exports of the completed DX17, DX18, DX19, and DX20 reports.
requirements.boundary_note: Final exported PDFs are independently requested deliverables and are not implied merely by editable-source delivery or source export capability.

requirements.title: Reusable Design Asset Package
requirements.definition: Provide the fonts, icons, logo files, colour codes, and other design assets needed to edit and export future reports consistently.
requirements.boundary_note: The supporting asset package is independently required even when editable templates have already been delivered.

unresolved_candidates.description: The client requests additional minor changes shown only in an unavailable attached image, so the affected Requirement boundaries and specific changes cannot be determined from message text.
